intended_object: The full subquiver of a graded linear quiver C on the objects satisfying a predicate P. Its objects are the objects of C satisfying P, and the hom module between two of them is the graded hom module of C between them. This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation, which describe it as the analogue of a full subcategory in the sense of Keller's A∞ categories.
explanation:
The definition is `InducedQuiver C Subtype.val`, where `InducedQuiver C F` is a one-field structure wrapping an element of the source type `D`. Its `GradedLinearQuiver` instance takes as hom module (and grading) from X to Y the one of C from `F X.obj` to `F Y.obj`. With `F = Subtype.val : Subtype P → C`, the objects are the elements of C satisfying P, and the hom modules and gradings are exactly those of C. That is the full subquiver.

This follows the way Mathlib builds full subcategories, as induced categories along `Subtype.val`. The construction works for any type C and any predicate P, so it is at full generality. The graded linear structure is attached through the instance, and it requires only what a `GradedLinearQuiver` already carries.

Mathlib has no notion of graded linear quivers, so it has no counterpart for this object. `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` is the analogous construction for categories, but it is a different object.
